display.title: How values are shown
display.asStored: Show every value as the database prints it
display.binaryHex: Hexadecimal, as the database prints them
display.timeZone: Time zone for values that have one
display.hint: Only how the grid shows values. Copies, exports, filters, edits and the search keep the database's own text; "Copy as displayed" in the cell menu copies what you see. A value with a time zone is converted to the zone you choose and shows its offset; one without is never converted. Masked columns stay masked.
display.patternHint: A pattern uses strftime's directives: %Y year, %m month, %d day, %b month name, %H hour, %I hour of 12, %M minutes, %S seconds, %.f fraction, %p AM or PM, %:z offset, %Z zone.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.hint: Applies to every workspace and is saved in your personal settings.
appearance.interfaceSizeHint: Scales the whole window: text, spacing, the explorer, dialogs and the results. The font sizes chosen for the editor and the results are at the normal size and grow with it; the editor's zoom then multiplies the editor's.
appearance.nullText: Show NULL as text (off: an empty cell)
appearance.gridHint: Only changes how cells are drawn: copies and exports keep the values.
appearance.resultTabs: Result tabs kept per editor tab
appearance.colorize: Color values by their type (numbers, text, dates, booleans, NULL)
appearance.headerType: Show each column's type in its header
appearance.headerComment: Show each column's comment in its header (a table's data)
appearance.gridFontSize: Font size of the results, in pixels
appearance.gridFontSizeHint: From {{min}} to {{max}}, at the normal interface size. Only the results: the editor has its own.
appearance.resultTabsHint: From 1 to {{max}}. Past it, the oldest result that is not pinned is closed; a run always shows every result it returns.

language.title: Language
language.label: Interface language
language.hint: Messages from databases and SSH servers are shown as they arrive.

explorer.title: Explorer
explorer.showSystemHint: System schemas (pg_catalog, information_schema, sys…) and the roles, users and logins built into each engine.
explorer.sortingHint: Without alphabetical order, names keep the order the database returns. Columns always keep their table's order. Folders first puts roles, users and the like before the schemas.
explorer.serverSideFiltersHint: A connection's filters go into the database's catalog queries, so a server with thousands of schemas or tables only sends what passes them. Turned off, every name is read and filtered on this computer; what you see is the same.

connections.title: Connections
connections.namePatternIntro: The add-connection form names a new connection with this pattern as you fill it in, until you type a name of your own.

variable.port: The port (the engine's default when left empty)
variable.database: The database, or a file's name without its extension
variable.engine: The engine's name, such as PostgreSQL
variable.env: The connection type's id, as chosen (dev, test, prod…)
variable.file: A SQLite or DuckDB file's name

connections.syntax: Click a variable to add it. {a|b} takes the first one with a value; a doubled brace writes a brace. An empty pattern suggests no name.
connections.hint: Only new connections: editing and importing from DBeaver keep their names.

types.title: Connection types
types.intro: A connection's type shows as a badge next to the connection and in its editor, and gives it safeguards. Types from the project are shared with your team; you can add your own and change any type's badge for yourself. Safeguards only add up: you can turn one on, but not off a safeguard the project or Production turns on.
types.deleteExplanation: Your type {{name}} ({{id}}) will be removed from this computer.
types.deleteUsed_one: This connection uses it and will keep the label without the type's color or safeguards:
types.deleteUsed_other: These {{count}} connections use it and will keep the label without the type's color or safeguards:
types.resetTitle: Undo your changes to this connection type?
types.resetExplanation: Your changes to {{name}} ({{id}}) will be removed from this computer: it goes back to its {{layer}} definition.
types.resetUsed_one: This connection uses it and will follow that definition again:
types.resetUsed_other: These {{count}} connections use it and will follow that definition again:
types.overrideHint: Your changes are saved in your personal settings and only apply on this computer.
types.name: Name
types.manualCommit: Start editor tabs with auto-commit off
types.manualCommitHint: Changes wait for Commit or Rollback; the tab can still turn auto-commit on.
types.smartCommit: Smart commit: switch to manual commit on the first change
types.smartCommitHint: The first statement that changes data opens a transaction that waits for Commit or Rollback; then the tab returns to auto-commit.
types.closeIdleHint: Nothing reconnects or runs again on its own. A connection with an open transaction is never closed.
types.inheritedHint: Greyed-out safeguards are turned on by the project or by Production and cannot be turned off.
types.maskColumns: Mask these columns on every connection of this type
types.maskInherited: The team's definition always masks: {{patterns}}. Yours add to them.
types.maskHint: One pattern per line (* is any characters, ? one). Patterns add up across the built-in, team and personal definitions, and no connection can leave them visible.

masking.title: Masking
masking.intro: Columns whose values show as •••••• on every connection on this computer: in the grid, copies, exports, statistics and agents' answers. One cell can be revealed at a time.
masking.saved: Saved. It applies to connections opened from now on.
masking.unreadable: user.toml could not be read, so every column of every connection is masked until it is fixed.
masking.hint: One pattern per line, ignoring case: * is any characters, ? one. A pattern matches a column's name or the table column it reads; table.column names the table too. A connection of your own can leave a column visible in its form; a connection from the repository cannot unmask these, and connection types can add their own. Masking keeps values off the screen, not away from SQL: an expression such as lower(email) gets past it, and so does an alias on SQL Server, DuckDB and SQLite on a server.

history.title: History
history.stored: Every query you run from the app is saved on this computer with its connection, time, duration, row count and error. Opening a saved query never runs it.
history.perConnection: Saving is set per connection: right-click a connection in the explorer, choose Edit… and look in Options. Turn it off before running SQL with passwords or other secrets. Turning it off keeps the queries already saved.
history.audit: This history belongs to the desktop app. Queries from AI agents (spelaiondb mcp) go to a separate audit log.

network.title: Network
network.profilesIntro: A network profile is how connections reach their databases: SSH hops, a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, or both. Many connections can share one; changing it changes all of them. Connections choose theirs in their SSH tab.
network.portsIntro: SSH tunnels listen on a local port of this computer (127.0.0.1). By default any free one is used.
network.loadFailed: Could not read the current range: {{error}}
network.saved: Saved. Tunnels opened from now on use it.
network.portsHint: Useful when a firewall or another tool only allows some ports. A connection with its own local port (in its SSH tab) keeps that one.

updates.title: Updates
updates.unavailable: Automatic updates are not available in this build yet. New versions are on the releases page.
updates.atStartup: Check for updates when the app starts
updates.manualDeb: This copy was installed from a .deb package: download the new .deb from the releases page and install it with your package manager.
updates.manualRpm: This copy was installed from an .rpm package: download the new .rpm from the releases page and install it with your package manager.
updates.manualDownload: This copy cannot update itself: download the new version from the releases page.
updates.hint: Updates are signed and installed only when you click “Install and restart”. Open tabs come back with their SQL, not run.

failed.install: Could not install the update: {{detail}}. Install again to retry.
failed.openReleasesPage: Could not open the releases page: {{detail}}
failed.setCheckAtStartup: Could not save the update setting: {{detail}}

updates.problemHint: Copies the version, the system, the plugins, the engines in use and the app log's last lines, with names, hosts, users, paths and secrets hidden, to paste into a GitHub issue. SpelaionDB sends nothing.
updates.diagnosticsError: Could not copy the diagnostic info: {{detail}}

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.intro: Database engines run as plugins: programs SpelaionDB starts for their connections. Only plugins built by SpelaionDB are listed here. Each one is checked against the signed plugin catalogue before it is installed, and again every time it starts.
plugins.off: Checking for updates is off, so the plugin catalogue is not read. The plugins inside the installer still work.
plugins.noCatalogue: No plugin catalogue has been accepted yet.
plugins.catalogueFailed: Could not read the plugin catalogue: {{detail}}. The plugins inside the installer still work.
plugins.refusedShipped: Version {{version}} inside the installer is not started: {{why}}
plugins.missing: Version {{version}} should be inside the installer, but {{program}} is missing.
plugins.removeSessions_one: It is running for {{engines}}: removing it stops it, and its {{count}} open session is lost.
plugins.removeSessions_other: It is running for {{engines}}: removing it stops it, and its {{count}} open sessions are lost.
plugins.removeRunning: It is running for {{engines}}: removing it stops it.
plugins.restartHint: Stops its process, giving it a few seconds to close its files: its sessions are lost and nothing is run again. The next connection starts it again.
plugins.restarted: Restarted: its sessions were lost. Reconnect a tab to start it again.
plugins.restartTransactions_one: Restarting it ends its sessions, and the open transaction in this tab is rolled back:
plugins.restartTransactions_other: Restarting it ends its sessions, and the open transactions in these tabs are rolled back:
plugins.restartAvoid: To keep the changes, cancel and commit first. Nothing is run again: reconnect each tab when you need it.
plugins.removeHint: Nothing you ran is run again. New connections use the build that is left, if any.
plugins.fileHint: A plugin archive (.tar.gz) is installed only if the accepted catalogue lists it with the same SHA-256. A catalogue file (.signed) is accepted only with SpelaionDB's signature, and never if it is older than the one kept.
plugins.fileTitle: Install a plugin or a catalogue

scripts.title: Scripts

mode.ask: Ask: stop, skip or skip all

scripts.onErrorHint: Each editor tab can choose another mode for its runs. A cancelled run always stops, and so does a failed statement that aborted or rolled back its transaction. Risky statements are still confirmed before the run.
scripts.notify: Notify me when a long run finishes while the app is in the background
scripts.notifyHint: The notification says which tab finished and whether something failed; it never contains SQL or data.
scripts.confirmDelayHint: In the confirmation of a risky statement (DROP, DELETE without WHERE, data changes on Production…), “Run anyway” stays disabled this long, so it is never pressed on reflex. 0 enables it at once. Which statements ask first is not changed.

editor.title: Editor
editor.restoreHint: Open tabs come back after a restart with their text and connection, disconnected: consoles and files, including unsaved changes. Their results are never kept.
editor.reconnect: Reconnect the last connections at startup
editor.reconnectHint: Only connects (it may ask for a password); nothing runs on its own.
editor.zoomHint: Multiplies the editor's font size and line height. In the editor, Ctrl+= zooms in, Ctrl+- zooms out and Ctrl+0 goes back to 100%. The sizes are at the normal interface size (Appearance) and grow with it.
editor.snippets: Type sel, ins or upd and press Tab to expand a snippet. Tab moves to its next field; Shift+Tab moves back. Your own snippets and the template of new scripts are in Settings › Snippets.

snippets.title: Snippets
snippets.hint: A snippet is text the editor inserts when you type its name and press Tab. Tab then moves to its next field and Shift+Tab back. Snippets are yours alone, kept on this computer, and are never run by themselves.
snippets.name: Name
snippets.nameHint: What you type before Tab: letters, digits and underscores. A built-in name (sel, ins, upd) replaces that snippet.
snippets.textHint: Fields are written ${1:name}, ${2:other}…; Tab visits them in order and ${0} is where the cursor ends.
snippets.full_one: You already have {{count}} snippet, the most allowed
snippets.full_other: You already have {{count}} snippets, the most allowed
snippets.loadFailed: The snippets could not be read: {{reason}}
snippets.templateLabel: Text a new script starts with
snippets.templateHint: Empty for none; saved when you leave the box. Only new query tabs start with it: files, history entries and generated SQL open as they are.

map.title: Map
map.tiles: Show map tiles from a tile server
map.tilesHint: Off by default. Every tile the map loads tells that server which part of the world you are looking at. Without tiles, shapes are drawn on a plain background and nothing leaves this computer.
map.tilesNeedServer: Give a tile server below first.
map.name: Name
map.urlHint: An https:// address with {z}, {x} and {y} where the server puts the zoom and the tile, as its documentation gives it (http:// only for a server on this computer). Check that its terms allow use from an app.
map.attributionHint: The credit the server asks maps to show. It is shown on the map.
